title: Say what you want in time
odia: ଚଇତା ! ତବତ ଖାଇବୁ କି ପଖାଳ ଖାଇବୁ ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ ଥାଉଁ କହିଥା
literal_meaning: Chaita! Will you eat hot food or pakhala? Say so while there is still time.
explanation: The pointed address and choice between hot food and pakhala turn a practical request into a memorable line: say what you want while another person still has time to arrange it. The dictionary marks Chaita as a non-respectful form of Chaitanya, so the tone can carry impatience or a dismissive edge. Applying it to other decisions is an editorial reading of the complete quoted example; its first occasion is unknown.
meaning_odia: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା କରିବାକୁ ହେଲେ ଆମ ଇଚ୍ଛାଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିବା ଦରକାର। ସବୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ସରିଗଲା ପରେ ମତ ବଦଳାଇବାଠାରୁ ସମୟରେ କହିଦେବା ଭଲ—ଏହି ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ବିଚାରଟି ଏଠି ଖାଇବା କଥାରେ ଆସିଛି।
english_summary: A meal cannot be arranged around an answer that arrives too late.
odia_summary: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି।
usage_example: A friend arranging a shared journey asks everyone to confirm their plans before tickets are booked. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The source identifies Chaita as a non-respectful or dismissive form of Chaitanya. No particular historical person or household is established. Pakhala remains a named food; the wording should not be softened into a uniformly polite request.
